## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence of the 68 docs relevant to these policies was traced to the base rule, an extended rule, a factor ladder, a compute line or a tool contract. Specific checks:

- Additions: none found. Items examined and judged entailed rather than added:
  - `escrow_shortage_projection_5a615eb3` line 2 "a bill whose month so found comes before month 1 is taken in month 1" — entailed by the source compute (`b0` subtracts a bill whose month index ≤ 0 in month 1); the rule prose is silent on it, so this is an equivalent restatement of the computed semantics, not added law.
  - `late_charge_measure_on_payment_7ff38bde` Basis Q&A "not the amount left unpaid and not the payment with its escrow deposit" — entailed by the baseline rule ("measured on the monthly principal-and-interest payment on the loan record"); it does not hint that a variation exists. Recorded as a reading risk only: it denies, in the baseline document, the inclusion the note-form factor applies to installment-note loans; a solver must resolve the two by the factor's specificity (I did in the blind pass).
  - `escrow_cushion_base_d6847265` "An expiry on the next payment due date itself is not earlier than it" — entailed by `DAYS(expiry, nd) > 0`.
  - Tool-card effect and receipt sentences — from the `task_tools.py` docstrings.
- Rewrites / omissions: none.
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …"): none. Each tool name occurs only in its own hub's invocation block.
- A task's opening world state written as policy fact: none (no seeded figure, name, date or status of either task appears in the corpus; checked the scored values, the record values and the members' names).

Policy-side notes (do not change this skill's verdict):
- PN1: the base measure `homeloan_msr_bill_paid` / `homeloan_msr_past_due_payments` tests a bill against `monthly_pi_amount` on record; after a rate change (this task: record 1156.80, bill billed at 3.875 with 1142.68 reversed) a bill re-booked at its reversed amounts stays below the record PI under that measure, while the shortage edge's `condition` uses "billed interest unpaid / shares booked again". The KB carries both as the source has them, and the replacement card's effect statement ("the reopened monthly payment shows as paid") makes the solution unique; the tension is in the source's definitions.
- PN2: base `homeloan_evt_returned_payment` states "If the reopened month is now past its grace period, its late charge is assessed under homeloan_evt_late_charge" — an inter-event order in base law, rendered verbatim as clause 3 of `returned_payment_rule_502b4f02`. Not a KB finding.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** Every atom of the four extended policies (rules, baselines, all 17 factor ladders with every tier), the governing base policies, the overwrites (retired clauses present and marked retired, none retired that the source did not retire, the unnamed clauses still in force), the three prerequisites and the four tool contracts are carried at the same strength; no added normative claim. First revision; no earlier revision to relate to.

## dependency_form

- Each of the three prerequisite sentences stands verbatim, state form, on its blocked side only (shortage hub; replacement hub twice). The "Restated:" lines are same-form equivalents in the same document — not findings. The replacement hub's restatement joins its own two sentences; both edges belong to that one blocked policy, so this is not an aggregation across problems.
- No state-form sentence restated as an action, performer or other problem (the shortage hub never names the replacement, the late charge or the returned fee; the replacement hub never names the two booking actions).
- No tool name outside its own hub; no route, step list, dependency table, checklist or chained example across problems; no wrong/right contrast across problems.
- Titles and openings name general subjects ("Paying a Rural Home Loans Escrow Shortage in One Sum", "Replacement Remittances for Reopened Monthly Payments", "Rural Home Loans Late Charge Booking", "Returned-Payment Fee Booking"); none mirrors the task situation (a bounced October payment, a shortage letter).
- Depended-on documents are reachable from the records' own words (reopened / returned / late charge / returned-payment fee); not only through the dependent hub's phrasing.
- Factor documents state ladders as rules, never which tier a member or most members fall on; no evidence row of the task written in. Factor documents that name another part of the figure (relief "before the charge is raised to its floor or lowered to the product's maximum"; owner relief "from the fee as limited by the size of the returned remittance"; fees-carried "added to its principal-and-interest and escrow shares"; carry-limit "the lower of the fees carried and the limit") carry the source's own order/assembly sentences and do not point at a document — not findings.
- Baseline documents carry no hint of modification ("unless otherwise", "adjustments may apply", exception lists, pointers): none found. The late-charge baseline Q&A noted under kb_to_source is a negative restatement of the baseline, not a hint.
- Base-law order statement (PN2) is recorded as a policy-side note, not here.

**KB-EXPLICIT PASS.**
